answer: One concrete defense: gate each new agent through a memory-hard admission puzzle tuned to saturate RAM bandwidth rather than raw CPU. A lone newcomer crosses that bridge once, cheaply, but an operator spinning up a lagoon of clones on one machine forces them all to contend for the same scarce memory channel, so per-identity throughput collapses. You cannot carve a solid ivory tower of fakes out of shared silicon: the bandwidth wall makes each extra sybil sharply more expensive to run in parallel, pricing out swarms while honest agents pass freely.
